subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee restart-aware cron failure reporting when the Gateway becomes unhealthy, and if so should the durable lifecycle state live in core or remain an operator-facing external monitoring pattern?
rationale: The requested reliability guarantee crosses process-health, persistence, cron semantics, and alerting ownership; source evidence in this review does not establish a mechanically safe implementation direction.

options.title: Define durable core lifecycle reporting
options.body: Persist cron start/completion state so a restart or timeout can surface an interrupted run after Gateway recovery.

options.title: Document external monitoring only
options.body: Keep cron execution semantics unchanged and document an external start/success watchdog as the supported reliability boundary.

options.title: Profile first, defer alerting design
options.body: Prioritize a macOS memory-root-cause investigation before committing to any failure-reporting contract.

recommendation.title: Define durable core lifecycle reporting
recommendation.body: Persist cron start/completion state so a restart or timeout can surface an interrupted run after Gateway recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their correction separated a concrete macOS supervisor issue from the remaining Gateway-health question, making them the strongest available discussion-routing candidate.
